purpose: Classify duplication before treating analyzer output as debt.

questions.prompt: What should we call this SSOT context? (stable id, e.g. c2004 or my-service)
One sentence: what reuse problem are you trying to settle?
Which languages are in play? (comma-separated: python, javascript, typescript, go, rust, other)
How is the shared code packaged today? (comma-separated: git-submodule, npm, pip, vendored-copy, monorepo-path, facade-reexport, unknown)
List the trees or files that look like copies (comma-separated repository-relative paths).
Do those trees share the same git remote (same upstream package, checked out twice)?
If they are git checkouts, are they pinned to the same commit?
Must the copies stay byte-identical (parity-gated), or may they drift?
Do the copies implement different protocols or APIs on purpose?
If they may diverge, what is the documented KNOWN_DIVERGENT reason? (empty if identical)
What is the canonical owner? (git remote, package name, or module path)
If a facade re-exports the canonical module, what is the facade path? (empty if none)
Can every consumer import the SSOT package without coupling a standalone product to another monorepo?
Is there a duplication or complexity analyzer report (code2llm TOON, redup, jscpd)?
If yes, which analyzer? (code2llm-toon, redup, jscpd, other, none)
Does the report look noisy? (CC on constants, docs as god modules, generated proto, minified assets, same-file fuzzy matches)
Has a human confirmed this pair is real debt, not analyzer noise or a generated mirror?
Existing parity or pin test path, if any (empty if none).
